title: Graded release quarantining and automated rollback orchestrator for private control-plane upgrades
creator: Marta Gonzalez
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) control-plane upgrades are high-risk: tenant-specific networking, operator-managed RBAC, and stateful operators mean mistakes cause tenant outages or long rollbacks. Current staged promotion flow relies on manual gating and ad-hoc traffic slicing which is slow and error-prone.

Goal: Build an automated, graded release quarantining and rollback orchestrator that integrates with our Terraform IaC modules and control-plane lifecycle tooling. The orchestrator must: 1) create an isolated quarantine cohort (tenant set) for early verification; 2) run semantic compatibility checks, infra diffs and synthetic traffic suites; 3) automatically promote or quarantine further cohorts based on telemetry and deterministic health rules; 4) trigger fast automated rollbacks if predefined safety signals breach thresholds.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full RBAC/SSO rework, non-control-plane component upgrades (will be separate tickets), and multi-region cross-tenant migrations.

Non-functional requirements: end-to-end upgrade should be observable in Console with <5m detection-to-decision latency for critical regressions, and automated rollback completion within 15 minutes for cohorts under 100 tenants. Must work with our Terraform modules and produce reproducible planned-state artifacts for auditing.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can create and manage a quarantine cohort using Terraform workspace isolation and tagging
Terraform plan diffs are captured and correlated to a release ID and stored in an artifact store for auditing
A semantic compatibility check runs prior to promotion (API schema, KV cache format, operator CRD annotations) and fails fast on mismatches
Synthetic traffic harness runs against quarantine cohort and reports pass/fail per preconfigured suites
Promotion rules support metric-based gating (latency, error-rate, saturation) and time-based hold windows
Automated rollback can be triggered by rule breach and completes without manual intervention for cohorts <100 tenants
Console dashboard shows cohort health, prom metrics, and a clear trace from a failed request back to the upgrade change set
Runbook generated automatically when a rollback is triggered with links to Terraform plan, GitHub PR, and relevant logs
approach_notes:
We will implement a controller that coordinates three subsystems: 1) IaC Manager - uses Terraform Cloud/Enterprise API and modular workspaces to materialize a quarantined control-plane variant; 2) Verification Engine - runs a chain of validators (terraform-diff gating, schema checks, operator compatibility tests, synthetic workloads); 3) Promotion Orchestrator - applies gating rules and invokes either promotion, staged expansion, or rollback.

Key design choices: prefer immutable promotion artifacts (release ID + terraform plan) over in-place patches to simplify rollbacks. Use a small, isolated tenant cohort (configurable) as first-quarantine. Store telemetry snapshots (last 15 minutes) and evaluate with a deterministic rule engine to avoid heuristic drift. Expose a manual override for SRE on the Console.

Trade-offs: immutable artifacts increase storage and planning time but simplify safe rollback and audits. Tight coupling to Terraform Cloud API reduces portability but gives strong audit trail and plan visibility; long-term we'll add a generic IaC adapter.

Compatibility notes: must be compatible with existing KV cache migration scripts (see ENG-39281) and the version catalog service (see ENG-12147).

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Terraform plan drift between quarantined and promoted environments. Mitigation: capture and sign plans as release artifacts and verify apply results against the signed plan before promotion.

Risk: False positives from synthetic traffic leading to unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require multi-metric confirmation (latency + error-rate + CPU saturation) and a configurable cool-down window before auto-rollback.
Risk: Long rollback times for large cohorts. Mitigation: limit first automated rollbacks to cohorts <100 tenants and provide a staged parallel rollback pathway for larger sets.
Risk: Secrets/KMS handling during quarantines. Mitigation: use tenant-scoped ephemeral secrets and ensure KMS policy tags are propagated by IaC Manager; security review required.
